common_name: Bee's Knees Petunia (Compact Yellow Petunia with Violet-Purple Blush)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Bee's Knees was the first petunia to win an AAS Gold Medal since 1950, chosen for its unusually consistent color and weather resistance.

directions: Bee's Knees bears soft yellow flowers washed with a violet-purple blush radiating out from the throat, a bicolor pattern distinct from the solid or veined yellows already in this dataset. The plant forms a neat, self-branching mound rather than a sprawling trailer, holding its shape without pinching and resisting the stem breakage that heavy rain and wind cause in looser-habited petunias. It self-cleans continuously through summer heat into cooler autumn weather with no deadheading required, and its strong stems and consistent color made it an AAS Gold Medal winner. Grow in full sun with regular fertilizing for the longest, densest bloom display.

common_name: Tidal Wave Hot Pink Petunia (Vigorous Hot Pink Mounding-Trailing Petunia)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Tidal Wave Hot Pink'

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; space 12 inches apart for a dense mounded hedge or 24 inches or more apart to let it spread as a groundcover.

directions: Tidal Wave Hot Pink is the newest color added to the award-winning Tidal Wave line, carrying some of the brightest, richest pink tones in the series on 2 to 2.5 inch blooms, distinct from the cherry-red and pale lilac-silver Tidal Wave selections already cataloged here. Like its series-mates it grows into a tall, mounding plant that trails outward rather than staying low and flat, reaching roughly 15 inches tall while spreading up to several feet wide when given room. It shows strong tolerance to botrytis, recovers quickly after heavy rain, and resists lodging, holding its shape through summer storms better than many trailing petunias. Use it as a dense summer hedge in tight spacing or as a sprawling groundcover and large container filler when spaced wide.

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun for the strongest flower production.

directions: Supertunia Limoncello carries soft, butter-yellow flowers accented by deeper yellow veins that make the bloom pop, a gentler pastel take on yellow petunia breeding than the clear grandiflora yellow of Prism Sunshine already in this dataset. Its mounding, trailing habit stays lower and more compact than the outsized Vista series, making it a dependable spiller for combination planters, window boxes, and hanging baskets. The plant is heat and drought tolerant, self-cleans without deadheading, and attracts butterflies and hummingbirds. Grow in full sun for best flower coverage over a long bloom season.

common_name: Cascadias Rim Magenta Petunia (Magenta-Purple Petunia with Cream Picotee Edge)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; give the cascading habit room to spill over basket or bed edges.

directions: Cascadias Rim Magenta bears large, trumpet-shaped flowers in dark purple to magenta red, precision-edged in a cream picotee rim that can take on a chartreuse cast, a crisp bicolor pattern not found among the solid-colored petunias already in this dataset. Bred by Danziger, the vigorous, cascading habit is well suited to hanging baskets, window boxes, patio containers, and spilling over border edges. Plants flower prolifically from early summer through the first frost and show strong heat and drought tolerance once established. Grow in full sun for the heaviest bloom and the most defined edge coloring.

common_name: Sophistica Blackberry Petunia (Near-Black Burgundy Grandiflora Petunia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in well-drained soil kept evenly moist but never waterlogged, in full sun; Sophistica Blackberry is part of PanAmerican Seed's designer collection of large-flowered grandiflora petunias in unusual, saturated colors.

directions: Sophistica Blackberry is described by its breeder as the blackest petunia available from seed, with shimmering burgundy-black trumpet blooms carrying reddish-purple undertones rather than the true reds, pinks, and yellows of the other petunias already cataloged here. It forms a dense, upright, herbaceous plant that reads best massed together, where the unusual near-black coloring shows to full effect against lighter companion plants. Flowering runs from mid spring to late summer, and the plant does best in average to evenly moist soil, since it will not tolerate standing water. Give it full sun for the darkest, most saturated bloom color.

common_name: Amore Queen of Hearts Petunia (Red and Yellow Bicolor Heart-Patterned Petunia)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Amore Queen of Hearts'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil; this Danziger-bred Amore series selection tolerates part shade better than many sun-hungry petunias.

directions: Amore Queen of Hearts produces red trumpet-shaped flowers striped with yellow that converge at the base of each petal to form a distinct heart shape, a novelty bicolor pattern unlike any solid or veined petunia already in this dataset. The dense, mounded plant stays compact and floriferous from mid spring to mid fall, making it a strong performer in hanging baskets, window boxes, and mixed containers. It tolerates full sun to partial shade better than many petunia selections and draws butterflies and hummingbirds while being largely ignored by deer. Blooms self-clean continuously, requiring no deadheading to stay tidy and full through the season.

common_name: Aloha Kona Sunshine Calibrachoa (Golden Yellow Semi-Upright Million Bells)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; give acidic, sharply drained potting mix, since calibrachoa suffers iron chlorosis quickly in alkaline soil.

directions: Aloha Kona Sunshine bears bold, golden-yellow flowers on a semi-upright, mounding plant that holds its shape a bit more than the strictly trailing habit typical of Superbells and Callie selections already in this dataset. It is part of the Aloha Kona series, bred for a bold range of colors from white through orange, purple, and hot pink, and this yellow selection thrives through summer sun and heat without fading. Blooms are self-cleaning and appear continuously from late spring through fall with no deadheading required. Regular acid-forming fertilizer keeps the color vivid and prevents the iron chlorosis common to calibrachoa grown in neutral or alkaline mixes.

common_name: MiniFamous Double Amethyst Calibrachoa (Double-Flowered Plum-Purple Million Bells)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; this Selecta-bred series performs well in both hanging baskets and window boxes thanks to its dense, trailing habit.

directions: MiniFamous Double Amethyst produces fully double, frilly flowers in a deep plum-purple, a richer and more textured bloom form than the single, flatter faces of the Superbells and Callie selections already cataloged here, and a distinct color from the blue-purple of MiniFamous Neo Double Blue and the ruby-red of MiniFamous Uno Double Red. Growth is dense and trailing, eventually spilling well over the edges of hanging baskets and mixed containers as the season progresses. The double blooms hold up better to wind and rain than thin-petaled single calibrachoa and require no deadheading, self-cleaning continuously from late spring to early fall. Grow in full sun to partial shade with acidic, well-drained soil and regular acid-forming fertilizer.

common_name: Callie Peach Calibrachoa (Peach Trailing Million Bells with Scarlet-Ringed Throat)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after hard freeze danger has passed; the Callie series from Syngenta is bred for compact-to-medium vigor, making it a good fit for smaller hanging baskets and combination pots.

directions: Callie Peach bears soft peach flowers with a yellow throat ringed in scarlet, a warmer, more layered color pattern than the flat dark red of Callie Dark Red or the clear pink of Callie Rose already in this dataset. Part of Syngenta's Callie breeding line, which has collected more than 30 trial awards since its 2005 introduction, it forms the same compact, trailing habit as its series-mates, staying tidy in smaller hanging baskets and combination pots. Flowers bloom continuously from late spring to early fall and self-clean without deadheading. Regular acid-forming fertilizer sustains the peach and scarlet coloring through the heat of summer.
